what_its_for: Mometasone furoate is a steroid medication that reduces inflammation (swelling and irritation) in your body. Depending on the form you are using, it can treat nasal allergy symptoms like stuffy or runny nose and sneezing (nasal spray), asthma (inhaler), or skin conditions like eczema, psoriasis, and rashes (cream or ointment). It works by calming down the immune system response that causes these symptoms.
how_to_take: How you use this medicine depends on the form you have been given. NASAL SPRAY: Blow your nose gently first. Shake the bottle well and tilt your head slightly forward. Insert the tip into one nostril while closing the other, then spray while breathing in slowly through your nose. Repeat for the other nostril. Avoid blowing your nose right after using it. INHALER (for asthma): Breathe out fully first, then place your lips around the mouthpiece and inhale deeply and steadily. Hold your breath for about 10 seconds, then breathe out slowly. Rinse your mouth with water and spit it out after each use to prevent mouth infections. CREAM or OINTMENT (for skin): Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area only. Wash your hands before and after applying. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages unless your doctor tells you to. Do not use on your face, groin, or underarms unless specifically directed by your doctor.
dosing: Your doctor will tell you the exact dose that is right for you. Typical doses are: NASAL SPRAY (adults and children 12 and older): 2 sprays in each nostril once a day. Children 2 to 11 years: 1 spray in each nostril once a day. INHALER (asthma): Usually 1 to 2 puffs once or twice a day, as directed by your doctor. CREAM or OINTMENT: Apply a thin layer to affected skin once daily. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for the one you missed. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store all forms of mometasone at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not freeze the nasal spray or inhaler. Keep the nasal spray upright when not in use. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medications down the toilet unless the instructions say to do so. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of medicine you no longer need.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting the nasal spray or cream in your eyes or mouth. If this happens, rinse thoroughly with water. Do not use more than your prescribed dose, as using too much steroid medicine can cause side effects. Avoid close contact with people who have active infections like chickenpox or measles, as steroid medicines can weaken your immune system with long-term use. For skin cream, avoid applying to broken, infected, or irritated skin unless your doctor tells you it is safe. Do not stop using the inhaler suddenly without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better, as this could make your asthma worse.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; signs of a fungal infection in your mouth or throat such as white patches, soreness, or pain (mainly with inhaler use); changes in your vision such as blurred vision or seeing halos; signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst or frequent urination (with long-term use); nose bleeds that are severe or do not stop (with nasal spray); skin thinning, stretch marks, easy bruising, or wounds that heal slowly (with skin cream); unusual weight gain, swelling, or extreme tiredness; any new or worsening symptoms. Also call your doctor if your condition does not improve after a few weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: The time it takes to feel better depends on the form you are using. NASAL SPRAY: Most people notice some improvement within 1 to 2 days, but it may take up to 1 to 2 weeks of regular use to get the full benefit. Use it every day as prescribed, even if you feel better. INHALER (asthma): This medicine is for daily prevention, not for sudden breathing attacks. It may take 1 to 2 weeks to notice improvement in your asthma symptoms. Always keep a fast-acting rescue inhaler with you for sudden attacks. CREAM or OINTMENT: Skin symptoms may start to improve within a few days, but it could take 1 to 3 weeks to see the full effect.
special_populations: PREGNANCY and BREASTFEEDING: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Use it only if your doctor decides the benefit outweighs any possible risk. CHILDREN: Mometasone nasal spray can be used in children as young as 2 years old for allergy symptoms. The inhaler is approved for children 4 years and older for asthma. Children using steroid medicines long-term should have their height and growth monitored regularly by their doctor. ELDERLY: Older adults generally use this medicine safely, but should still be monitored for side effects, especially skin thinning when using the cream. PEOPLE WITH INFECTIONS: Tell your doctor if you have any current infections, including fungal, bacterial, or viral infections, before starting this medicine. PEOPLE WITH LIVER DISEASE: Use with caution, as liver problems may affect how your body processes this medicine. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all your medical conditions and all medicines you are taking.
